question: Why do nurses wear masks in the hospital?

options.A: To keep warm in air-conditioned rooms
options.B: To prevent patients from seeing the nurse's facial expressions
options.C: To eliminate the need for hand washing
options.D: To stop airborne and droplet germs from spreading

explanation: Masks act as a shield to keep harmful germs from traveling through the air between patients and staff. You've got this!

question: What is the main difference between droplet and airborne germs?

options.B: Airborne germs cannot infect healthcare workers
options.C: Droplet germs need negative pressure rooms
options.D: Droplet germs travel on heavy particles that fall quickly, while airborne germs stay floating longer

explanation: Think of it by weight! Heavier droplets drop fast to the ground, but tiny airborne particles float around longer and need stronger masks.

question: What is the main job of a regular surgical mask?

options.B: To filter out tiny microscopic viruses completely
options.C: To block large splashes, sprays, and droplets
options.D: To provide a tight, air-sealed fit around the face

explanation: Surgical masks are great shields against everyday hospital splashes and sprays, even though they don't seal tightly around your face.

question: Why can't a regular surgical mask protect you against true airborne diseases like TB?

options.A: The loose fit lets air and tiny germs slip in through the edges
options.B: The material dissolves in humid hospital rooms
options.C: They only block bacteria, never viruses
options.D: They are only made for patients to wear

explanation: Since surgical masks aren't tightly sealed, air takes the easiest path—right around the sides instead of through the filter!

question: What percentage of tiny particles must an N95 respirator filter out?
explanation: The '95' in N95 simply means it catches a minimum of 95 percent of test particles. Simple and reliable!

question: A male nurse with a thick beard is caring for a patient with TB. What should he do?

options.A: Shave his beard so the N95 can seal properly
options.B: Wear an N95 right over his beard
options.C: Wear a standard surgical mask instead

explanation: Facial hair prevents that crucial tight seal. Shaving ensures the N95 can properly protect him from airborne germs.

question: What kind of mask do you need when entering a patient's room who is on droplet precautions?
explanation: For droplet precautions, a standard surgical mask is all you need to block those larger splashes and secretions.

question: Why do nurses wear masks during sterile procedures like putting in a central line?

options.A: To comply with fire safety codes
options.B: To protect the nurse from inhaling meds
options.C: To stop the nurse's germs from contaminating the sterile field
options.D: To keep their face warm in cold rooms

explanation: Here, the mask protects the patient! It stops your own mouth and nose bacteria from getting into the sterile area.

question: What is the quick check a nurse does every time they put on an N95 to check the seal called?
explanation: It is a quick self-check you do every single time you put on your respirator to make sure it is sitting right.

question: Why do healthcare workers need to do an N95 fit test every year?

options.A: Weight changes or dental work can change how the mask seals
options.B: Manufacturers change their plastic formulas yearly
options.C: Hospital rules just want to renew licenses
options.D: Filters expire chemically after one year

explanation: Our faces change over time! A fit test ensures your mask still seals safely against your unique face shape.

question: Which part of a used mask is safe to touch when taking it off?

options.B: The bottom edge near the chin
options.C: The straps, ties, or ear loops

explanation: Always grab the straps! The front of the mask holds onto trapped germs and should never be touched directly.

question: Why should you wash your hands right after taking off your mask?

options.B: To remove germs that may have touched your hands if you brushed the outer mask
options.C: To prevent mask elastic from marking your fingers
options.D: To cool your skin down after a long shift

explanation: Hand hygiene right after removal breaks the chain of infection just in case your fingers brushed against outer germs.

question: Why is pulling your mask down around your neck during a break a bad idea?

options.B: It stretches out the elastic bands forever
options.C: It contaminates the clean inside of your mask with germs from your neck skin
options.D: It blocks blood flow to your head

explanation: Pulling it to your neck exposes the inner lining to skin oils and germs, which you then breathe right back in!

question: Your surgical mask becomes damp and sweaty during a busy shift. What should you do?

options.A: Leave it on because moisture helps filtration
options.B: Flip it inside out so the dry side faces out
options.C: Remove and discard it, clean your hands, and put on a fresh one
options.D: Wipe it with paper towels and pocket it

explanation: Once a mask gets damp, its filter barrier stops working well. Swap it out for a fresh one to stay safe!
